mkp-diagrams:graph@1.name: graph
mkp-diagrams:graph@1.about: Nodes and the connections between them, in layers, top down or left to right: a pipeline, a process, an org chart, a state machine. Choose a node to light it and its connections.

inputs.name: nodes
inputs.about: each node: its id and label; a kind (start, end, process, step, decision, actor, artifact, metric, focus, io, subprocess, usecase, label) sets its icon, tone, shape and note, and icon (a name, or none), tone (info, ok, warn, bad, accent, neutral), shape (card, pill, oval, io, label) and note override it; group is the box it sits in; detail is said in the bar when it is chosen

inputs.name: edges
inputs.about: connections between node ids: a label on the line; a dashed or dotted line; muted, drawn quieter; back, against the main flow (a retry), so it doesn't count for the layers; arrow, a head at the target

inputs.name: groups
inputs.about: boxes for nodes to sit in, each with a title

inputs.name: dir
inputs.about: top down, or left to right

inputs.name: kind
inputs.about: what kind of diagram it is, said small before the title

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: the title

value.expr: filter(edges, e => indexof(ids, e.from) >= 0 and indexof(ids, e.to) >= 0)

values.name: plain

value.expr: map(filter(good, e => not e.back), e => {from: e.from, to: e.to})

comment: a link that closes a cycle, or is marked back, doesn't count for the layers, so a cycle can't

value.expr: filter(ids, id => len(filter(plain, e => e.to == id and e.from != id)) == 0)
filter(plain, e => not (near[e.to] <= near[e.from] and levels(ids, [e.to], plain)[e.from] < 1000))

value.expr: filter(map(range(0, depth), r => map(filter(nodes, n => rank[n.id] == r), n => n.id)), l => len(l) > 0)

values.name: links

value.expr: map(good, e => {from: e.from, to: e.to, label: e.label})

comment: an edge that spans layers runs through a lane in each layer it crosses, and a labelled one puts
its label beside its lane in a row of its own (route.mkp)

values.name: loopy

value.expr: map(good, e => e.back or (near[e.to] <= near[e.from] and levels(ids, [e.to], plain)[e.from] < 1000))

comment: left to right, a line back sits first in each column it crosses, over the lines going on, so it
meets its ends level with them instead of from below

value.expr: backfirst(lay.rows, flatten(map(filter(range(0, len(good) - 1), k => loopy[k]), k => lay.via[k])), dir == right)
